purpose: Bound the final content-independent hardening pass before substantial corpus-dependent development.

research.title: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 2 Rev. 1 — Developing Cyber-Resilient Systems
research.use: Resilience framing: anticipate, withstand, recover, adapt.

research.title: NIST AI Resource Center / TEVV
research.use: Evaluation and TEVV pattern source; no conformity claim.

research.title: NIST TEVV-Athlon
research.use: Evaluation framework pattern source; no conformity claim.

research.title: AWS Well-Architected Reliability REL 12
research.use: Recovery, scale, resiliency/chaos, and game-day testing pattern source.

scenarios.title: Bounded large archive load envelope
scenarios.nextAction: Increase the bounded synthetic corpus in controlled tiers and record throughput/resource observations without claiming production capacity.
scenarios.limitations: Current PIT-0 load is a bounded engineering fixture, not a production-capacity guarantee.

scenarios.title: Branch topology preservation
scenarios.nextAction: Retain as a regression invariant when adversarial fixtures are added.

scenarios.title: Logical attachment reference de-duplication
scenarios.nextAction: Retain one-observation-per-logical-reference semantics in future fixtures.

scenarios.title: Unknown or novel source shapes remain explicit
scenarios.nextAction: Add adversarial archive fixtures proving unknown object shapes are reported/quarantined rather than silently invented.

scenarios.title: Orphan or missing-parent topology is handled explicitly
scenarios.nextAction: Add branch fixtures with missing parents and prove the importer preserves/reports the anomaly without fabricating ancestry.

scenarios.title: Invalid timestamp and ordering anomalies are explicit
scenarios.nextAction: Add invalid/missing/out-of-order timestamp fixtures and define fail/warn preservation behavior.

scenarios.title: Repeated and partially changed point-in-time exports classify without deletion inference
scenarios.nextAction: Keep five-way PIT classification and absence-is-not-deletion semantics in the PFC regression set.

scenarios.title: Exact archive import is idempotent
scenarios.nextAction: Retain exact-input idempotency in archive regression coverage.

scenarios.title: PIT comparison receipt reuse is idempotent
scenarios.nextAction: Retain deterministic receipt reuse for identical comparison inputs.

scenarios.title: Interrupted archive import can be safely retried
scenarios.nextAction: Add an executable process/interruption-and-retry proof around archive ingestion.
scenarios.limitations: Operational contract exists; an explicit kill/retry executable proof is still required.

scenarios.title: Downstream derivation failure cannot corrupt immutable source evidence
scenarios.nextAction: Inject a bounded archive-derivation failure after source acceptance and prove source/archive evidence is unchanged and replayable.

scenarios.title: Automatic retry authority is bounded and cannot loop indefinitely
scenarios.nextAction: Retain retry-budget and current-evidence checks as a cross-system invariant.

scenarios.title: Conversation interruption reconstruction preserves recoverable truth
scenarios.nextAction: Retain interruption reconstruction as a cross-system recovery invariant.

scenarios.title: Synthetic database recovery path is executable
scenarios.nextAction: Reuse SDN recovery proof patterns for future PFC failure injection rather than creating a parallel recovery framework.

scenarios.title: Stale lease or lost owner is fenced and reclaimable
scenarios.nextAction: Retain lease fencing/reclaim verification as the concurrency ownership invariant.

scenarios.title: Provider timeout/failure after durable reservation has a bounded recovery path
scenarios.nextAction: Map existing provider recovery tests to reservation/settlement invariants and add any missing exact failure fixture.
scenarios.limitations: Existing provider recovery substrate is present, but PFC has not yet certified the exact cross-system invariant.

scenarios.title: Schema or version mismatch fails closed
scenarios.nextAction: Add stale/newer-schema fixtures for the archive/history and one additional critical subsystem; require explicit unsupported/fail-closed result.

scenarios.title: Evidence artifact write failure does not erase primary truth
scenarios.nextAction: Inject artifact-output failure after a successful primary operation and prove the source/DB truth remains durable while evidence publication is marked incomplete.

scenarios.title: Archive ingestion throughput is measured on bounded synthetic tiers
scenarios.nextAction: Capture elapsed time, records/sec, fixture identity, and environment for at least two bounded corpus tiers.
scenarios.limitations: Functional load exists; standardized performance observations are not yet captured.

scenarios.title: Conversation History list/search/detail latency is measured
scenarios.nextAction: Add bounded synthetic latency measurements for list/search/detail at multiple corpus sizes.

scenarios.title: PIT comparison throughput is measured
scenarios.nextAction: Add bounded timing and row-count observations for unchanged and changed synthetic exports.

scenarios.title: Database and index growth is measured
scenarios.nextAction: Record table/index size deltas for bounded synthetic corpus tiers in isolated PostgreSQL.

scenarios.title: Concurrent ingestion/retrieval behavior is measured and bounded
scenarios.nextAction: Add a small deterministic concurrency fixture that establishes safe behavior and explicit unsupported load beyond the measured envelope.

scenarios.title: Conversation History reader works across supported staged deployment states
scenarios.nextAction: Retain pre/post archive-analytics staged reader compatibility in CHIST acceptance.

scenarios.title: Critical migrations have exact object/authority verification
scenarios.nextAction: Inventory migration verifiers and close any P0 migration lacking an exact postcondition check.
scenarios.limitations: CHIST has strong exact verification; PFC has not yet established repository-wide critical-migration coverage.

scenarios.title: Stale schema fails closed before unsafe work
scenarios.nextAction: Create an executable stale-schema fixture for at least archive/history and one runtime subsystem.

scenarios.title: Canonical bootstrap/current schema parity is demonstrated for P0 subsystems
scenarios.nextAction: Inventory bootstrap-vs-forward-migration parity and add a machine-checkable comparison for P0 subsystems.
scenarios.limitations: Existing lane-specific verification exists; repository-wide parity is not yet certified by PFC.

scenarios.title: Conversation History roles enforce least privilege
scenarios.nextAction: Keep history reader/certifier/deriver negative privilege checks in the PFC security set.

scenarios.title: Private history evidence is excluded from ordinary Data API roles
scenarios.nextAction: Retain anon/authenticated/service_role exclusion checks.

scenarios.title: Synthetic archive evidence cannot qualify as the real certified baseline
scenarios.nextAction: Retain explicit certification authority and real-baseline guard semantics.

scenarios.title: Purpose-specific credentials do not silently fall back to generic database authority
scenarios.nextAction: Promote existing purpose-specific credential assertions into a reusable negative test contract.
scenarios.limitations: CHIST documents and tests this boundary; PFC has not yet generalized the negative contract.

scenarios.title: Private source material cannot leak into logs or generated test artifacts
scenarios.nextAction: Add synthetic canary secrets/content and assert they do not appear in workflow logs or shareable artifacts outside explicitly authorized evidence.

scenarios.title: Exact-head workflow stall/failure state is classified
scenarios.nextAction: Retain exact-head lane health observation and resolved-state behavior.

scenarios.title: Notification authority remains separate from remediation authority
scenarios.nextAction: Retain separate observer/notification/retry authority and bounded retry proof.

scenarios.title: Last-known-good checkpoint remains recoverable after interruption
scenarios.nextAction: Unify checkpoint evidence expectations across conversational and operational work without introducing a new checkpoint store.
scenarios.limitations: Strong lane-specific checkpoint/recovery evidence exists; cross-system operator contract is not yet frozen.

scenarios.title: Original failure evidence survives recovery/retry
scenarios.nextAction: Select representative archive, Foundry, and lane-health failures and prove recovery appends evidence rather than replacing the original failure.
scenarios.limitations: Existing systems are append-oriented, but PFC has not yet certified this across representative subsystems.

scenarios.title: Conversation History retrieval is chronological and branch-aware
scenarios.nextAction: Retain branch-aware retrieval proof on synthetic history.

scenarios.title: Source evidence and derived evidence remain explicitly distinct
scenarios.nextAction: Retain provenance-separated readback and no-fabrication behavior.

scenarios.title: Large-history pagination/cursor behavior is deterministic
scenarios.nextAction: Add synthetic list/search pagination or cursor tests with deterministic tie-breaking.

scenarios.title: Context/result assembly is bounded
scenarios.nextAction: Convert existing memory-context bounds into a reusable measurable retrieval contract for PFC.
scenarios.limitations: A bounded context design exists; PFC has not yet measured generic history/retrieval assembly across corpus tiers.

scenarios.title: Machine-readable cross-system coverage matrix exists
scenarios.nextAction: Keep the matrix versioned and update it only with evidence-bearing status transitions.

scenarios.title: Unsupported proven claims fail validation
scenarios.nextAction: Keep negative contract tests for missing and nonexistent proof references.

scenarios.title: Performance observations use a common evidence shape
scenarios.nextAction: Define the minimal versioned performance observation schema and use it in bounded scale fixtures.

scenarios.title: Semantic-quality evaluation framework
scenarios.nextAction: Design semantic-quality benchmarks only after certified corpus evidence or separately justified external research provides target meaning.
scenarios.rationale: Content-free engineering can validate deterministic mechanics but cannot establish whether inferred topics, salience, personality, or memory importance are semantically correct for the user's real corpus.
